title: Horizon sampler: deterministic workload garden and stable signal anchors for CI perf gates
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a deterministic, multi-axis workload sampler (Horizon sampler) and a set of stable signal anchors that provide robust CI performance gating across kernel-selection, attention scheduling, and prefill/decode trade-offs. Deliverables: 1) Horizon sampler CLI + library to synthesize workload shards across sequence-length, prefill:decode ratios, KV cache hit distributions, and quantization/kernel variants. 2) Canonical stable-signal anchor set (seeded inputs + expected telemetry fingerprints) for p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, memory, and kernel choice distribution. 3) CI job templates and perf gate rules that run ensemble runs and decide pass/fail with noise-tolerant thresholds. Success criteria: - Detect regressions >= 2% median latency or >= 5% tail shift consistently across hardware variants (A100/RTX/Tesla) - Reproducible within CI noise bounds on 5 repeated runs - Generate actionable kernel-selection diffs and example traces for investigation Approach: - Define a small but expressive parameter grid (sequence length buckets, context reuse patterns, batch shapes, kv-hit ratios) and a deterministic seed space so runs are repeatable. - Implement a scheduler that maps shards to runtime profiles and simulates prefill/decode handoffs to exercise attention-window optimizations. - Instrument kernel selection telemetry (which kernel chosen, input shape, quantization mode) and attach deterministic fingerprints for each anchor. - Integrate into CI with a two-stage run: quick smoke (single-run) and ensemble run (5 seeds) for gating. - Store anchor run artifacts in S3 and link to console dashboards for visual diffing Trade-offs and constraints: - Full production fidelity is expensive; we will focus on representative shapes that historically explain 80% of variance. - Hardware noise requires ensemble runs and median-of-medians logic rather than single-run thresholds. - Some kernels are non-deterministic across drivers; where necessary we normalize by kernel-choice probability rather than strict equality.
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with PM + Research. Agreed to prioritize sequence-length buckets (8, 64, 512, 2048) and prefill:decode ratios (100:0, 80:20, 50:50, 10:90).

2026-03-04: Initial prototype of sampler landed. PoC can generate 120 deterministic shards and schedule them across local runner. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/horizon-sampler
2026-03-05: Design review feedback from infra and reliability: add ensemble-run support and artifact retention policy. Action: add --seeds and --artifact-prefix flags to CLI.

2026-03-07: First ensemble run on A100 dev pool. Observed p95 shift of +3.2% after kernel reorder change PR #2345. Created investigation ticket ENG-555912 to root cause. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
2026-03-08: CI integration draft in runtime CI. Added perf-gate script that computes median-of-medians across seeds. Draft pipeline: https://ci.redwood.com/pipelines/runtime/horizon-sampler

2026-03-09: UX/Console sync. We will push anchor diffs to a new dashboard slice in Console under 'Perf Anchors' with thumbnails for kernel distributions and latency heatmaps. Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Horizon+Sampler+Spec

2026-03-10: Blocker: flaky driver-level timing on the shared dev pool causing 0.8% noise. Mitigation: run T=3 extra warmup runs and mark first as warmup in the artifact. Next step: coordinate a reserved quiet window on Dedicated pool for canonical anchor captures.
